title: They'll be there by now
goal: Make confident assumptions with -DIr, and say how sure you are with the right adverb.

intro.text: In conversation, `-DIr` on a guess says you're confident: *Şimdiye kadar varmışlardır* (They'll have arrived by now), *Duymuşsundur* (You'll have heard). Adverbs tune the certainty: *kesinlikle* and *mutlaka* (surely), *muhtemelen* (probably), *galiba* (I think), *belki de* (perhaps).

vocab.en: to be wrong, to be mistaken
I think, I believe (sanmıyorum: I don't think so)

exercises.question: Your friends left Ankara at eight; it's now noon. Which sentence makes a confident assumption?

why.1: *Vardılar* states it as a fact you know.
why.2: *Varmışlar* passes on something you heard, or a result you can see.

exercises.explain: `-mIş` + `-DIr`, *varmışlardır*: **they'll have arrived by now**. You're confident, though you haven't checked.

exercises.en: You'll have heard this news too.

accept: sundur

reject.why: *Duymuşsun* reports what you heard or what someone noticed. The assumption needs `-DIr` after the ending: *duymuşsundur*.
*Duymuştur* is **he** or **she**. For **you**, the ending *-sun* comes first: *duymuşsundur*.

exercises.explain: `-(I)yor` + `-DIr`: a confident guess about what is going on now.

exercises.question: Which sentence says **I'm sure you've heard: it was all over the news**?
options: Belki de duymuşsundur; bütün haberlerde vardı.

why.1: *Belki de* (perhaps) is far too weak for **I'm sure**.
why.2: *Galiba* (I think, it seems) is a soft guess.
why.3: *Hiç duymamışsındır* says **you'll never have heard of it**.

exercises.label: *duymak*, **must have heard, will have heard**: I must have heard, you'll have heard…

accept: duymuşumdur
duymuşsundur
duymuştur
duymuşuzdur
duymuşsunuzdur
duymuşlardır

exercises.explain: The type I ending comes first, then `-DIr`, which follows harmony and becomes *-tur* after ş: *duymuştur*.

exercises.title: Havalimanında
exercises.passage:
Elif saatine baktı: “Murat'ın uçağı yarım saat önce inmiş olmalı. Şimdiye kadar bavulunu almıştır.”

“Sanmıyorum,” dedi Can. “İstanbul'da hava çok kötüydü. Uçak büyük olasılıkla geç kalkmıştır.”

“Bu da olası. Ama mesaj da atmadı. Telefonunun şarjı bitmiştir; zaten her zaman bitiyor.”

Birkaç dakika sonra ekranda bir yazı belirdi: İstanbul uçağı tahminen bir saat gecikmeli. Can gülümsedi: “Gördün mü? Ben hiç yanılmam.” Elif omuz silkti: “Peki. Ama Murat'ı tanırım: şu anda uçakta mutlaka uyuyordur.”
exercises.translation: Elif looked at her watch: “Murat's plane must have landed half an hour ago. He'll have collected his suitcase by now.” “I don't think so,” said Can. “The weather was very bad in Istanbul. The plane most likely took off late.” “That's possible too. But he hasn't sent a message either. His phone's battery will have run out; it always does anyway.” A few minutes later a notice appeared on the screen: the Istanbul flight is delayed by roughly an hour. Can smiled: “See? I'm never wrong.” Elif shrugged: “All right. But I know Murat: he's surely asleep on the plane right now.”

questions.q: What does Elif assume at first?
options: Murat has collected his suitcase by now
questions.explain: *Şimdiye kadar bavulunu almıştır*: an assumption with `-DIr`.

questions.q: Why does Can think the plane is late?
options: The weather in Istanbul was very bad
He read it on the screen
questions.explain: *Hava çok kötüydü. Uçak büyük olasılıkla geç kalkmıştır.*

questions.q: How does Elif explain the missing message?
options: His phone's battery has probably run out
questions.explain: *Telefonunun şarjı bitmiştir*: an assumption based on what she knows of him.

questions.q: What is Elif sure of at the end?
options: Murat is asleep on the plane

exercises.task: A friend hasn't answered your messages since yesterday. Write three or four sentences to another friend guessing why, from the most likely reason to the least. Use `-DIr` at least twice, and at least three of these: *mutlaka, muhtemelen, büyük ihtimalle, galiba, herhâlde, belki de*.
models: Murat dünden beri cevap vermiyor. Muhtemelen işte çok yoğundur; bu hafta önemli bir toplantısı vardı. Belki de telefonunu evde unutmuştur. Herhâlde akşam arar.

Selin'den hâlâ haber yok. Büyük ihtimalle telefonunun şarjı bitmiştir; her zaman şarj etmeyi unutuyor. Galiba hafta sonu köye de gidecekti; orada internet çekmiyordur. Merak etme, mutlaka yarın yazar.
checklist: `-DIr` after a tense or an ending: *yoğundur*, *unutmuştur*, *çekmiyordur*
Adverbs in order of strength: *mutlaka* and *büyük ihtimalle* before *galiba* and *belki de*
No clash: *kesinlikle* and *mutlaka* don't go with *olabilir*

exercises.question: Which is the most cautious?
exercises.explain: *Belki de* (perhaps) is the weakest; `-DIr` keeps the guess, the adverb sets its strength.
